name: Arman
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Rishes, L. D. 1947. Armanskij dialekt evenskogo jazyka. PhD thesis, Leningrad Institute of Language and Thought
earlier_scan.note: Sole substantive description of Arman (divergent Even variety), unpublished Soviet thesis, not accessible.

sources.citation: Badgaev, N. B. 2008. O nekotorykh foneticheskikh javlenijakh i ikh vozmozhnom substratnom proiskhozhdenii v jazykakh Sibiri v areal'nom osveshchenii. Oriental Studies (Cyberleninka).
sources.note: Areal phonetics of Siberia; Arman named only as a 'sibilant' Even dialect that keeps original initial s-. No stress.

sources.citation: Janhunen, Juha & Tapani Salminen. 1993-2000. UNESCO Red Book on Endangered Languages: Northeast Asia, entry 'Even: Arman' (compiler J. Janhunen, 16 Dec 1993).
sources.note: Sociolinguistic entry (extinct; 'an archaic variety of Even.. perhaps to be classified as a transitional idiom between the two languages'); only source named is Doerfer 1978. No stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page arma1243 (Hammarström et al.), with references Rishes 1947, Kazama 2003, Novikova 1960: 20, Whaley 2012, Doerfer 1978: 18-19.
sources.note: Classification only (Tungusic > Ewenic > Arman; extinct). Comment: Arman 'did not partake in a sizeable set of sound changes involving initial consonants'. No stress.

No stress statement. English article's reference list yielded the modern sources: Alonso de la Fuente 2014 (review of Armanisches Wörterbuch, WZKM 104: 412-417, JSTOR 24361819), Malchukov 2023 'Ewen' (Routledge, pp. 261, 288), Hölzl 2018 handout p. 6, Cincius 1965 CAJ 10: 152-153, Aralova 2015: 5-6.

sources.citation: Petrov, A. A. 2025. Iz istorii dialektologicheskikh issledovanij evenskogo (lamutskogo) jazyka. Art Logos (Cyberleninka).
sources.note: History of Even dialectology. 'V 1947 g. L. D. Rishes.. sovershila ekspeditsii k armanskim evenam, podgotovila i zashchitila kandidatskuju dissertatsiju na temu «Armanskij dialekt evenskogo jazyka». Issledovatel' otmetila, chto armanskij dialekt zanimaet osoboe polozhenie, sokhranjaet rjad arkhaichnykh chert, sblizhajushchikh ego s evenkijskim (tungusskim) jazykom.' Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Pakendorf, Brigitte & Natalia Aralova. 2020. Even and the Northern Tungusic languages. In M. Robbeets & A. Savelyev (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Transeurasian Languages. Oxford: OUP. Author manuscript, HAL hal-02889683.
sources.note: Section 18.3 Phonology covers Even segments and harmony; a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing. Arman named once, in classification footnote 3 (Northeastern group 'comprising Even and extinct Arman', citing Li & Whaley 2009: 525). Nothing on Arman stress.

sources.citation: Aralova, Natalia. 2015. Vowel harmony in two Even dialects: Production and perception. LOT Dissertation 400. Utrecht: LOT.
sources.note: Phonology is of Ola (Eastern) and Bystraia Even, not Arman. Arman appears only in the dialect-classification survey, pp. 5-6: 'The question if the now extinct Arman variety has a dialectal status or is a separate language cannot be answered.' No stress statement for Arman.

sources.citation: Languages of Siberia (lingsib.iea.ras.ru) Even page and Even bibliography.
sources.note: One sentence: the Arman dialect, spoken in the 1940s by about 10 people in Ola and Arman', has disappeared. Bibliography lists Rishes only as author of Even primers and the Cincius & Rishes dictionaries (1952, 1958); no Arman work, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Malchukov, Andrej. 2023. Ewen. In A. Vovin, J. A. Alonso de la Fuente & J. Janhunen (eds.), The Tungusic Languages, 261-ff. London: Routledge.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Modern sketch with a phonology section; mentions Arman (pp. 261, 288). Would give the current Ewen stress statement against which any Arman note could be compared.

sources.note: Grammar of the Ola dialect, Arman's immediate neighbour (the last Arman speakers lived at Ola); p. 20 discusses Arman; its phonetics chapter gives the Eastern Even stress rule that Arman is most likely to share.
